subtopics.title: Inflation Defined and the CPI Basket

questions.question: Which price movement qualifies as inflation?
options: A sustained and significant rise in the general price level over time
A once-off jump in prices after a fuel-levy increase
School shoes becoming dearer while televisions become cheaper
A weekend special ending at one supermarket

questions.question: Inflation slows from 8% to 5%. Prices are:
options: Falling — this is deflation
Still rising, but more slowly — this is disinflation
Frozen by the Reserve Bank
Rising faster than before

questions.question: Housing carries a bigger weight than movie tickets in the CPI because:
options: Housing prices rise faster than ticket prices
The Reserve Bank considers housing more important
Household surveys show families spend a far larger share of their money on housing
Movie tickets are not sold in all provinces

questions.question: Analysts read the PPI as an early warning for the CPI because:
options: The PPI excludes services
The PPI is published a week earlier each month
The two indices use the same basket
Factory-gate price increases usually reach retail shelves a few months later

questions.question: The base-year basket cost R5 000; the identical basket now costs R5 400. The index reads:
The CPI climbs from 108,0 to 114,5 in a year. The inflation rate is:
options: About 6,0% — the 6,5-point change divided by the OLD index of 108,0, times 100

questions.question: Food (weight 40%) rose 12%, transport (35%) rose 4%, education (25%) rose 8%. Weighted inflation is:
A nurse's salary rises 5% while inflation runs at 7%. In real terms her salary has:
options: Risen by 5%
Risen by 12%
Stayed unchanged
Fallen by roughly 2% — more rands, but a smaller trolley

questions.question: Demand-pull inflation is best described as:
options: Total spending growing faster than the economy can produce — too much money chasing too few goods
Producers passing higher input costs on to consumers
The state fixing maximum prices
A stronger rand making imports cheaper

questions.question: Which list contains ONLY cost-push causes?
options: Consumer credit booms, wide government deficits, export surges
A weaker rand raising import prices, electricity tariff hikes, wage deals outrunning productivity
Cheap loans, rising bonuses, investment booms
Falling interest rates and higher grant payments

questions.question: Told in curve language, cost-push inflation appears as:
options: Aggregate demand shifting right — prices up, output up
Aggregate demand shifting left — prices down
Aggregate supply shifting left — prices up, output DOWN
Both curves shifting right at the same time

questions.question: Stagflation pairs rising prices with:
options: Rising output and falling unemployment
Falling prices in the following year
A budget surplus
Falling output and rising unemployment

subtopics.title: Consequences and the Fight Against Inflation

questions.question: During inflation, wealth is redistributed from:
options: Creditors to debtors — loans are repaid in rands that buy less
Debtors to creditors
Wage earners to pensioners
Shareholders to property owners

questions.question: A saver earns 5% interest while inflation runs at 7%. The real interest rate is:
options: Minus 2% — nominal rate minus the inflation rate

questions.question: Under inflation targeting, the Reserve Bank must keep CPI inflation:
options: Equal to the repo rate
At zero
Inside the 3-to-6-percent band, using the repo rate as its main instrument
Below the growth rate of GDP

questions.question: Raising the repo rate is a weak weapon against cost-push inflation because:
options: Commercial banks do not follow the repo rate
It automatically weakens the rand
Cost-push inflation cures itself
Higher interest rates cannot lower production costs — they only crush demand, at the cost of output and jobs

subtopics.title: The Trolley That Tells the Truth

questions.question: The contents and weights of the CPI 'trolley' are decided by:
options: Surveys of what households genuinely spend on, with bigger spending items taking more space
The prices retailers wish to advertise
A vote in parliament each budget
Only the cost of food and fuel

questions.question: The index stamp reads 108. This means:
options: The trolley costs R108
What cost R100 at the starting line now costs R108
Inflation is 108%
Prices fell by 8%

questions.question: A family insists prices rose far more than the official rate. Both claims can be true because:
options: Statistics South Africa only collects prices in one province
The official rate ignores food entirely
The official trolley is a national average, and no real household's spending matches the average
Shops charge different prices to different families

questions.question: The fingerprint of demand-pull inflation is:
options: Busy shops, empty shelves, order books full and delivery dates slipping
Quiet shops with rising prices
Prices falling across the economy
A stronger rand and cheaper imports

questions.question: Diesel climbs, the electricity tariff jumps and a drought shrinks the maize crop — while customers spend no more than before. This fire is:
options: Demand-pull inflation
Cost-push inflation — the producer's own bills rose, so shelf prices rise in self-defence
Deflation
Creeping demand inflation

questions.question: Turning the repo-rate 'hose' on a cost-push fire mainly:
options: Makes diesel and electricity cheaper
Restores the maize harvest
Drenches the shoppers while the cost pressure stays — sales fall and jobs go
Strengthens wage bargaining power

questions.question: An essay must diagnose the TYPE of inflation before recommending policy because:
options: Longer diagnoses earn more marks
Both types respond identically to the repo rate
The type changes every month
The cure depends on the cause — the repo rate fights demand-pull well and cost-push badly

subtopics.title: Who Wins and Who Loses When Prices Run

questions.question: The clearest LOSERS from inflation are:
options: Pensioners on fixed incomes, savers earning below inflation, and workers without bargaining power
Households repaying large bonds
Owners of property and shares
The government, as the biggest borrower

questions.question: A borrower quietly gains from inflation because:
options: Banks write off debts during inflation
The loan is repaid in rands worth less than the rands originally borrowed
Interest rates always fall when prices rise
Inflation increases the size of the loan

questions.question: The target band sits at 3 to 6 percent rather than zero because:
options: Zero inflation is illegal under the constitution
The band matches the GDP growth rate
A small, steady rise keeps the economy's wheels turning, while double digits destroy planning and trust in money
Banks require the band to set prime

questions.question: Zimbabwe in 2008 is the textbook case of:
options: Successful inflation targeting
Disinflation
Bracket creep
Hyperinflation — prices doubling within days until people abandoned the currency
